dossier:
There is a moment burned into World Cup folklore that belongs entirely to Cameroon. Italia 1990, Roger Milla comes off the bench, scores, and saunters to the corner flag with a shimmy that somehow managed to be both ridiculous and iconic at the same time. That dance wasn't just celebration — it was a declaration. The Indomitable Lions became the first African side to reach a World Cup quarter-final, and in doing so they didn't just represent Cameroon, they gave an entire continent permission to dream big on the grandest stage.

The decades since have been a rougher ride. Cameroon have qualified seven times in total, but that 1990 magic has proved stubbornly unrepeatable. They've arrived at tournaments with squads full of genuine talent and left early, victims of inconsistency, the odd controversial refereeing decision, and sometimes themselves. The Lions can be breathtaking one half and baffling the next — which, honestly, makes them one of the most compelling sides to follow at any World Cup.

For 2026, there is real reason for optimism. Bryan Mbeumo is quietly becoming one of the most dangerous forwards in Europe, André-Frank Zambo Anguissa brings elite-level control and physicality in midfield, and André Onana — for all the drama that has followed him — remains a goalkeeper capable of winning games single-handedly. At a home-continent-adjacent tournament with expanded places, the Lions aren't just showing up. They're hunting something.
whatToWatch: Watch Cameroon on a good day and you'll see football that feels alive — fast, physical, and completely unpredictable in the best possible way. If Mbeumo and Anguissa click in the same rhythm, casual fans are in for a proper show.
xFactor: Bryan Mbeumo, because he has the kind of low-centre-of-gravity trickery and cold-blooded finishing that can turn a tight knockout game on a single touch.
verdict: Cameroon will be the tournament's most exhilarating gamble — capable of genuinely stunning someone fancied, and equally capable of breaking your heart in the group stage.
funFacts: Cameroon won back-to-back Africa Cup of Nations titles in 2000 and 2002, yet those golden generations never managed to recapture the World Cup quarter-final heights of the Roger Milla era.

At the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, Cameroon became the first African team to beat Brazil in a World Cup match — a 1-0 win in the group stage — though they still went home in the group phase on goal difference.
name: Cameroon
